frase_inicial: Samantha and kids: retirement, college and the 2030 house are all drawing on the same cash.

tarjetas.frente: Retirement savings run out too soon
tarjetas.reverso: If you keep saving into taxable accounts only, the plan shows your invested savings and cash won’t support the lifestyle planned through old age. That means you’d need to cut spending, sell assets or change the plan later.
tarjetas.detalle: Projection: savings and investments run out at age 73; planned unpaid spending by end of plan about $1,448,673.

tarjetas.frente: College costs start very soon for Ethan
tarjetas.reverso: Ethan’s payments begin first and take the same cash you might use for retirement. Paying college from cash reduces the cushion that handles surprises and long-term saving.
tarjetas.detalle: College funding still needed beyond current balances: $98,837.55 total for both children.

tarjetas.frente: Yearly cash flow is slightly negative now
tarjetas.reverso: Right now you spend a bit more than comes in after saving. That gap chips away at the emergency cushion if near-term goals keep hitting the account.

tarjetas.frente: Big part of your wealth is the house and not spendable
tarjetas.reverso: Owning the home outright gives stability but doesn’t help pay bills or college unless you sell or borrow against it. Relying on the house is not the same as having ready cash.

tarjetas.frente: Homeowners and auto cover look missing in the records
tarjetas.reverso: The plan flags the house and car as uninsured. If those underlying policies aren’t in place, a claim could hit the liquid savings you’d rather keep for goals.
tarjetas.detalle: Top recommended move: add homeowners insurance on primary home to close coverage gap.

tarjetas.frente: A large chunk of investments sits in one US stock position
tarjetas.reverso: Having most of your investable money tied to a single broad US stock fund and heavy tech exposure raises the risk that a market shock would shrink the pot you plan to live on.
tarjetas.detalle: VTI is ~39% of investable; suggested move: reduce to 25% (about $58,300) for concentration band.

tarjetas.reverso: You’ve built saving in taxable accounts, but not yet in tax-advantaged accounts. Moving some saving into those accounts would change how long your money lasts and the tax you pay.
tarjetas.detalle: Eligible: up to $7,500 to deductible traditional IRA and up to $4,400 to HSA if health plan qualifies; current contributions 0.

tarjetas.frente: Most of your cash will be spoken for in the near term
tarjetas.reverso: After setting aside the vacation and Ethan’s near payment, only a very small cushion remains above the emergency reserve. That leaves little room if extra bills or college costs come sooner.
tarjetas.detalle: Accessible cash $80,000 covers 7.9 months before near-term goals and 6.1 months after; cash above reserve and goals $750.

tarjetas.frente: Buying a new home in 2030 will change monthly cash needs
tarjetas.reverso: The planned purchase brings a large down payment and a new mortgage payment that will compete with college and retirement saving. It’s another decision that forces tradeoffs.
tarjetas.detalle: Planned purchase value about $562,754 in 2030; planned loan $450,203.52 at 7% with monthly payment ~$2,995.

tarjetas.frente: You already have strong life and disability protection
tarjetas.reverso: Life insurance and disability are sized to protect Ethan and Ava if your income stops, so protection isn’t the thing you need to change first. Keep those premiums in the yearly budget.

movimientos.title: Close a coverage gap
movimientos.action: Add homeowners insurance on Primary home so coverage integrity clears that gap

movimientos.title: Reduce single-name concentration
movimientos.action: Bring VTI from 39% to 25% of investable for the next concentration band — about $58,300 of that line

movimientos.title: Reduce growth allocation toward glide
movimientos.action: Move the invested mix from 85% to 80% growth (glide 80%) for the next horizon-fit band — about $17,100 of the invested book

mapa.aviso: Illustrative simulator: it shows the direction of change, not a Sherpas projection.

siguiente_paso.razon: The plan’s top ranked move is to close a coverage gap on your primary home because the house and car show as uninsured and a claim would force you to use savings meant for college or retirement.
pasos: Find current homeowner policy documents or log into your insurer account to confirm coverage
If no policy, call two insurers for quotes and ask about adding the existing umbrella on top
Choose the policy with comparable coverage and set up the yearly premium in your budget
